Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (Verdant VP Eng), Evan Li (Verdant SRE), Sandra Ortiz (Verdant Head of Product)

Summary:
Follow-up postmortem to the 2026-09-28 production incident where Verdant experienced degraded inference availability on their dedicated Redwood cluster. Goal: review root cause, verify mitigations, agree rollout and monitoring changes, and assign owners for reliability improvements.

Topics:
- Root cause recap
- Short-term mitigations and patch status
- Long-term reliability changes (canary, circuit breaker, RBAC, observability)
- Next steps / owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick check we have the right folks? Maya, Evan, Sandra from Verdant?
[00:06] Maya Thompson: yep this is Maya, thanks alex, we got the invite and we were briefed by evan so good to go
[00:10] Priya Rao: cool, i'll kick off with the technical recap and then we'll go into mitigations, sound good?
[00:15] Evan Li: yep thanks, appreciate it
[00:18] Priya Rao: ok so short recap — on 9/28 we saw a spike of 503s and token generation failures when we pushed a model variant and a runtime rollout overlapped with autoscaler activity on Verdant's dedicated pool. the immediate trigger was a KV cache invalidation race: some nodes started serving with schema v2 keys while others still had v1, which caused the runtime kvcache lookup to miss and attempt a full state reload. that load path triggered increased memory usage, one of the dedicated gpu nodes hit oom, the autoscaler cycled a few nodes, and routing policy fell back but the fallback routing was misconfigured to a model alias that had an incompatible tokenizer — so requests failed.
[00:58] Sandra Ortiz: sorry to interrupt, can you repeat the routing fallback bit? i remember that caused a lot of our traffic to pile up on the control plane
[01:04] Priya Rao: sure — in short, the policy set to fallback to a hosted variant used the alias name 'verdant-prod-fallback' — but that alias was pointing to a newer tokenizer-bundled variant. tokenizer mismatch caused preprocessing to fail at the beginning of the pipeline which manifested as 5xx. normally the fallback should route to a compatible binary.
[01:26] Maya Thompson: so there's both a runtime cache mismatch and an alias/configuration issue, got it. is the cache mismatch purely a Redwood runtime bug?
[01:33] Priya Rao: yes, our investigation shows the patch we rolled out had a subtle key-versioning change. we didn't fully gate the key schema migration on a canary that exercised cross-node routing. in hindsight that was a rollout mistake.
[01:44] Alex Chen: i'll own the rollout process fix, but priya can you summarize the code patch status?
[01:49] Priya Rao: sure — patch is done, it adds backward-compatible key parsing and a short-lived transitional mode that accepts v1 and v2 keys, plus a deterministic GC to avoid simultaneous large state reloads. we've run unit and integration tests internally, and we pushed an internal build to staging yesterday. no regressions so far but we want to validate with Verdant traffic in canary.
[02:12] Evan Li: what's the plan for canary? we need to be sure we won't impact latency or cause another cascade
[02:18] Priya Rao: recommended plan: small percentage traffic (2-5%) to a canary subset of nodes, fixed concurrency limits, and explicit circuit-breaker so that if mem usage or p50 latency spikes the canary traffic is drained quickly. also keep the fallback mapping locked to a compatible model.
[02:34] Sandra Ortiz: we also want audit logs and full traces for any canary request, so we can replay and debug quickly if something goes wrong
[02:40] Priya Rao: absolutely — Redwood Console will emit trace IDs, model route details, and token-level latency breakdowns. we'll enable extended tracing for the canary window and ship the logs to Verdant's logging endpoint and to Redwood's support bundle.
[02:52] Maya Thompson: on the autoscaler flapping — can we throttle scale-down during rollouts? that seemed to exacerbate the problem
[02:59] Priya Rao: yes we have an autoscale policy you can pin for rollout windows: min replicas, cooldown extension, and a temporary disable for scale-to-zero. we'll propose a rollout policy in the doc.
[03:08] Alex Chen: ok let's talk timeline and responsibilities
[03:10] Priya Rao: Patch build is ready for canary, we can schedule the canary for Wed 2026-10-06 at 10:00 PT, pending Verdant approval. the canary will run for 2 hours with extended monitoring, then we'll increase to 10% for 4 hours if everything looks good.
[03:25] Evan Li: wed morning works for us, but we need the support bundle and the exact RPCs/metrics to watch, can you list those?
[03:32] Priya Rao: yes, we'll provide a checklist: memory/GC events, p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation error rates, KV cache hit/miss ratios, GPU utilization, and route alias resolution logs. we'll also attach a span-by-span trace map for a failing request.
[03:49] Sandra Ortiz: on governance — we need SSO logs and audit entries for any config change, and confirmation the patch won't change data residency or KMS usage
[03:56] Samir Patel: noted — Redwood maintains audit logs and the patch does not change KMS interfaces. we'll provide SOC 2 attestation excerpts and the security review doc.
[04:05] Maya Thompson: great. can you also run a simulated traffic replay to validate cache behavior? we have historical traces from the incident window
[04:11] Priya Rao: yes, we can replay your trace against the staging cluster with the patch; that will be part of the pre-canary validation.
[04:17] Evan Li: we'll prepare a sanitized replay and share it by monday EOD along with the logs we pulled from the incident
[04:22] Priya Rao: perfect. one more long-term item: we're recommending a few platform-level reliability improvements — canary-by-route, deterministic cache migrations with version markers, circuit-breaker at the routing tier, and improved model alias validation on the control plane.
[04:36] Alex Chen: and on Redwood side we'll add an automatic alias-compatibility check during rollouts to prevent incompatible fallback mapping.
[04:43] Maya Thompson: that's good, also please include runbook steps for our oncall. last time there was confusion about who should revert vs who flips the alias
[04:50] Samir Patel: we'll produce a one-page runbook — revert model, pin autoscaler, and contact tree for escalations.
[04:56] Sandra Ortiz: OK, any blockers to the canary?
[04:59] Priya Rao: we need the replay and logs from Verdant and Verdant's approval for Wed canary window. also Samir needs to finalize the support coverage for the window.
[05:08] Evan Li: we'll get the replay by monday and i'll confirm coverage by tuesday EOD
[05:13] Alex Chen: great — recap of next steps in chat and action items in the calendar invite. thanks everyone
[05:18] Maya Thompson: thanks all
